Here is a focused 7-day deload plan that preserves the same exercise selection, but reduces volume and intensity to promote recovery while maintaining technique and movement habits. It’s designed to be implemented after your 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy and just before ramping into an intensification block.

Overview
- Goal: Reduce fatigue, maintain movement patterns, preserve strength, and support recovery.
- Structure: Same exercises as your recent program, but lower total sets, lower RPE, and shorter sessions.
- Frequency: 5 days of training, 2 rest/recovery days (or 4–5 days with lighter sessions depending on schedule). If your plan previously used 4–5 sessions/week, keep a similar cadence with lighter loading.

Session design principles
- Use 40–60% of previous week’s loading for main lifts, or RPE 6–7 where possible.
- Keep tempo controlled (2-0-2-0 or 3-1-1-0) to emphasize technique and time under tension without excessive fatigue.
- Maintain full range of motion; prioritize form over load.
- Favor higher frequency of movement cues and mobility work.

Proposed weekly structure (example with 5 sessions)
- Day 1: Upper body (bench pattern)
- Day 2: Lower body (quad-dominant)
- Day 3: Rest or light cardio/mobility
- Day 4: Upper body (pull/push split)
- Day 5: Lower body (posterior chain emphasis)
- Days 6–7: Rest or active recovery

Detailed deload plan
Note: If your typical sessions were 18 working sets per session, this deload targets roughly 40–50% of volume, with lower intensity. Adjust according to how you feel.

Day 1 – Upper 1 (bench-focused)
Main lifts (lower volume, lower intensity)
- Bench Press: 3 sets x 5 reps at RPE 6 (about 60–70% 1RM)
- Overhead Press: 2 sets x 6 reps at RPE 6 (light to moderate)
Accessory/technique work
- Incline Dumbbell Press: 2 sets x 8 reps (RPE 6)
- Dumbbell Row or Seated Cable Row: 2 sets x 8 reps (RPE 6)
- Lateral Raises: 2 sets x 12 reps (RPE 6)
Core
- Plank: 3 x 30–45 seconds

Notes:
- Keep bench and press movement mechanics clean; pause lightly at the bottom if comfortable.
- Keep rest periods 60–90 seconds between sets.

Day 2 – Lower 1 (quad-dominant)
Main lifts
- Back Squat or Front Squat: 3 sets x 5 reps at RPE 6
Accessory/technique
- Leg Press: 2 sets x 8 reps (RPE 6)
- Walking Lunges: 2 sets x 8 reps per leg (RPE 6)
- Leg Extension: 2 sets x 12 reps (RPE 6)
Glute/hamstring
- Hyperextensions or Romanian Deadlift (light): 2 sets x 8 reps (RPE 6)
Core
- Farmer’s Carry: 2 rounds x 30 seconds

Notes:
- Use shallow depth if needed to maintain confidence and form, but strive for full ROM if comfortable.

Day 3 – Rest or Active Recovery
- Optional light cardio: 20–30 minutes easy pace
- Mobility/massage: 15–20 minutes
- Optional core work: 2 sets x 12–15 reps of anti-rotation exercises

Day 4 – Upper 2 (pull/push balance)
Main lifts
- Barbell Row or T-bar Row: 3 sets x 5–6 reps at RPE 6
- Push-ups or Dumbbell Floor Press: 3 sets x 6–8 reps at RPE 6
Accessory
- Seated Cable Face Pulls: 2 sets x 12 reps
- Dumbbell Hammer Curls: 2 sets x 10 reps
- Tricep Pushdowns (rope or bar): 2 sets x 10–12 reps
Core
- Pallof Press: 3 sets x 12 reps per side

Notes:
- Focus on scapular retraction and control during rows; avoid arching the back excessively.

Day 5 – Lower 2 (posterior chain emphasis)
Main lifts
- Deadlift (any style; conventional or sumo): 3 sets x 4–5 reps at RPE 6
Accessory/technique
- Glute-Ham Raises or Romanian Deadlift: 2 sets x 8 reps (RPE 6)
- Leg Curl: 2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Cable Pull-Throughs: 2 sets x 12 reps
Core
- Bird Dogs or dead bug: 3 sets x 12 reps per side

Notes:
- If deadlift form is not feeling stable, reduce load and maintain technique; the goal is injury-free movement.

Days 6–7 – Rest or Active Recovery
- If you’re feeling good, 20–30 minutes of light cardio or mobility work; otherwise full rest.

Training parameters and progression
- Volume: Target roughly 40–50% of previous average weekly sets. If you were doing 18 working sets/session, plan around 7–9 working sets for big lifts per session and 4–6 additional sets for accessories total per session.
- Intensity: Aim for RPE 6–7 on main lifts; never above RPE 7 on any movement during the deload.
- Tempo: 2-0-2-0 for compounds; 2-1-2-0 for some accessories if you want a slight tempo increase.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between lighter sets; 2–3 minutes for heavy main lifts if needed, but keep it brisk to maintain a deload feel.

Recovery and ancillary considerations
- Sleep: Target 7–9 hours per night; quality matters as much as duration.
- Nutrition: Maintain adequate protein (1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day). If training intensity is low, total calories can be maintained or slightly reduced; avoid large caloric deficits during a deload.
- Hydration: 3–4 liters/day (adjust for body size and climate).
- Mobility: Include 5–10 minutes of mobility work post-session focusing on hips, thoracic spine, shoulders.
- Stress management: Consider light activity on rest days (walks, mobility work, breathing drills) to aid recovery.

Optional adjustments
- If you’re extremely fatigued: reduce to 4 training days (Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat) with similar structure but even lower volume (2–3 sets per main lift, 6–8 reps) and shorter sessions.
- If you’re pressed for time: swap some accessory work to supersets, keeping overall volume low.

Progression into Week 1 of the intensification block
- After this deload, plan a gradual ramp into higher intensity or a more structured strength-focused phase. For example:
  - Week 1 of intensification: Increase main lift sets to 3–4 sets of 4–6 reps at RPE 7–8, preserving exercise selection.
  - Week 2–3: Add slight load progressions and maintain controlled volume, possibly reducing accessory volume to maintain overall load.

If you’d like, share your exact exercise list from the Week 4 hypertrophy block (the specific movements and approximate loads), and I’ll tailor the deload with precise loads and a per-session plan aligned to those numbers.

Great question. For a deload week, you want markers that are informative of strength/neuromuscular status but don’t impose large fatigue or risk of aggravation. Here are practical, low-fatigue options you can test that align with the week’s movements and keep you within the deload intent:

Recommended strength markers (deload-friendly)
- Floor press or bench substitute max reps at a controlled load
  - Pick a light-to-moderate load that you know you can quality reps with (e.g., 70% of planned 1RM floor press or neutral-grip press).
  - Test for max reps in 2 sets, then take the best single-rep effort as a rep-max proxy for chest/press strength.
  - Rationale: gives a chest/shoulder pressing capacity gauge without a heavy bench press.

- 3RM or 4–5RM on main hinge or squat pattern with reduced fatigue
  - Choose a main lift that’s already in your deload plan (e.g., floor press substitute, goblet squat or back squat with light load).
  - Do a single 3RM or 4–5RM attempt after warm-up if technique remains solid.
  - If unsure, use a rate-of-perceived-exertion target (RPE 7) and record reps at that load as a surrogate strength marker.

- Barbell row or chest-supported row rep max at a light load
  - Use a controlled 4–5 rep max test (or max reps in 5 sets of 4 reps with a light weight) to gauge pulling strength.
  - Keep sets low and tempo steady to minimize fatigue.

- Push-up or floor press endurance gauge
  - How many quality push-ups or floor press reps can you perform in a continuous set before technique degrades?
  - This tests muscular endurance in the pressing pattern but is low-fatigue if kept strict and controlled.

- Isometric strength check (time-held)
  - Isometric mid-thigh pull or push-press pin hold (e.g., hold a light-to-moderate weight at sticking point for 5 seconds, 3 attempts).
  - Useful for tracking explosive strength trends without accumulating fatigue.

- Mobility/technique + velocity proxy (accessible if you have basic tools)
  - If you have a linear position transducer or velocity-based device, you can do a light set of a main lift at a submaximal load and record mean velocity at 3–5 reps to gauge velocity drop vs. baseline from previous cycles (if you have data).
  - If not, you can do a simple time-under-tension and velocity cue (e.g., tempo 2-0-2-0 on a 5–6 rep set and note rep velocity by RIR).

How to implement within the deload plan
- Choose 2–3 markers to test this week that align with the deload lifts (e.g., floor press variant and barbell row or rack pull).
- Keep volume very low: 1–2 sets per test, with 2–4 reps per set at a controlled load.
- Maintain RPE targets for the week (main lifts at RPE 6; avoid pushing to failure).
- Record: weight used, reps completed, RPE, any technical notes, and a brief subjective fatigue score.

Data interpretation (quick guide)
- If your submaximal rep max on the press shows a small improvement or maintenance, that’s a positive sign heading into the intensification block.
- If pulling strength test shows a drop, consider dialing back volume in the upcoming weeks or ensuring mobility/shoulder health is prioritized.
- Track trend over weeks: you want to see stable or modest gains in these markers as you finish the deload and ramp into higher intensity.

Day 5 – Lower 2 (posterior chain emphasis) – uptick
- Deadlift (light-to-moderate): 3x4–5 (RPE 6–7; you can add a touch more weight than week 1)
- Glute-Ham/RDL: 1–2x8
- Leg Curl: 1–2x10–12
- Cable Pull-Through: 1–2x12
- Core (Bird Dogs/Dead Bug): 2x12 per side
Total: 9

Day 6 – Zone 2 Cardio 30 minutes
- 30 minutes steady-state cardio

Day 7 – Rest or Active Recovery
- Optional light cardio, mobility, or complete rest

Guidance for the push on Day 3 and Day 5
- Day 3: Keep the added work modest (2x6 on a floor press variant, 1x6 incline). Use a controlled tempo (2-0-2-0). Focus on technique and shoulder comfort.
- Day 5: Slightly heavier deadlift day (3x4–5 at RPE 6–7) but still within deload. If form wavers, back off by 1 rep or reset to RPE 6.
- Recovery support: emphasize scapular retraction, thoracic extension, and rotator cuff warm-ups before these sessions (5–7 minutes).

Monitoring and safety
- Watch shoulder symptoms. If any increase in pain or clicking/painful ROM, revert Day 3 push work to the original light level and don’t push further that day.
- Maintain sleep 7–9 hours and protein target 1.6–2.2 g/kg.
- Hydration and nutrition should support recovery; avoid large caloric deficits during the deload.

Communicate to the client
- Frame this as a controlled ramp in a deload context: “we’re holding the deload structure but with short, strategic increases to reinforce neuromuscular drive and keep you engaged.”
- Have him check in on shoulder comfort and perceived exertion after Day 3, then adjust Day 5 if needed.

If you want, share the exact load ranges you’ve been using in the week prior, and I can convert these adjustments into precise loads (percentages and rep targets) for each exercise so you have a fully numbered plan.

Here is the full deload week with all adjustments rolled in:

Assumptions
- Prior program: 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy, ~18 working sets per session.
- Deload target: ~40–50% of prior weekly volume, with movements preserved but loads and sets reduced.
- Shoulder-friendly chest emphasis replaces traditional bench press.
- Mobility day added (20 minutes) plus two Zone 2 cardio sessions.
- Midweek push progression on Days 3 and 5 to address boredom, kept within deload safety.
- Weekly structure: 7 days with 5 training/light activity days and 2 rest days (or adjust to your schedule; reflect this cadence).

Weekly structure at a glance
- Day 1: Upper 1 (shoulder-friendly chest emphasis)
- Day 2: Lower 1 (quad-dominant)
- Day 3: Mobility & Active Recovery + Light midweek push progression
- Day 4: Upper 2 (pull/push balance)
- Day 5: Lower 2 (posterior chain emphasis) – uptick in intensity relative to Day 2
- Day 6: Zone 2 Cardio 30 minutes
- Day 7: Rest or Active Recovery

Day-by-day plan with exact sets/reps and loads guidance

Day 1 – Upper 1 (shoulder-friendly chest emphasis)
- Dumbbell Floor Press (neutral grip or flat, depending on comfort): 3 sets x 5 reps at RPE 6
- Overhead Press (light, seated or dumbbell): 2 sets x 6 reps at RPE 6
- Incline Dumbbell Press: 1 set x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Dumbbell Row: 2 sets x 8 reps
- Lateral Raises: 1 set x 12 reps
- Plank: 2 sets x 30 seconds
Total working sets: 9
Notes:
- If shoulder irritates, reduce Overhead Press to 1 set x 6, or swap to a light Dumbbell Arnold press with a very light load.
- Tempo targets: 2-0-2-0 for all pressing movements; 2-1-2-0 for rows if desired.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between sets; 2–3 minutes for any heavier set if needed.

Day 2 – Lower 1 (quad-dominant)
- Back Squat or Goblet Squat (as needed for comfort): 3 sets x 5 reps at RPE 6
- Leg Press: 1 set x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Walking Lunges: 1 set x 8 reps per leg at RPE 6
- Leg Extension: 1 set x 12 reps at RPE 6
- Romanian Deadlift or Hyperextensions (light): 1 set x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Farmer’s Carry: 1 set x 30 seconds
Total: 9
Notes:
- If barbell back squat is uncomfortable, substitute goblet squat or DB front squat to preserve knee/hip drive.
- Focus on technique and depth within comfort.

Day 3 – Mobility & Active Recovery + Light Push Progression (midweek push)
- Mobility session: 20 minutes (as outlined previously; hips, thoracic, shoulders, ankles)
- Light push work (optional, total 3–4 extra working sets maximum):
  - Dumbbell Floor Press: 2 sets x 6 reps at RPE 7
  - Incline Dumbbell Press: 1 set x 6 reps at RPE 7
Notes:
- If shoulder fatigued, drop to RPE 6 or skip the extra push work entirely.
- Tempo: 2-0-2-0 for presses.
- This day should feel controlled and non-fatiguing.

Day 4 – Upper 2 (pull/push balance)
- Barbell Row: 3 sets x 5–6 reps at RPE 6
- Push-ups or Dumbbell Floor Press: 2 sets x 6–8 reps at RPE 6–7 (choose option that preserves shoulder comfort)
- Seated Cable Face Pulls: 1–2 sets x 12 reps
- Dumbbell Hammer Curls: 1–2 sets x 10 reps
- Tricep Pushdowns: 1–2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Pallof Press: 2 sets x 12 reps per side
Total: 9
Notes:
- If push movements aggravate, swap to a machine chest press with neutral grip and keep reps conservative.

Day 5 – Lower 2 (posterior chain emphasis) – uptick
- Deadlift (light-to-moderate, emphasize form): 3 sets x 4–5 reps at RPE 6–7
- Glute-Ham Raise or Romanian Deadlift (light): 1–2 sets x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Leg Curl: 1–2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Cable Pull-Through: 1–2 sets x 12 reps
- Core (Bird Dogs or Dead Bug): 2 sets x 12 reps per side
Total: 9
Notes:
- If deadlift form is unstable, drop to 3x4 at RPE 6 or reduce to 3x3 with a lighter load.

Day 6 – Zone 2 Cardio 30 minutes
- Zone 2 cardio: 30 minutes continuous (walk, cycle, or row at a comfortable but steady pace)
Notes:
- Keep the effort conversational; you can break into two 15-minute blocks if needed by schedule.

Day 7 – Rest or Active Recovery
- Optional light cardio, mobility work, or complete rest
Notes:
- Use this day to check in on shoulder comfort and overall recovery. Hydrate, sleep, and nutrition remain important.

Strength markers testing (deload-friendly and non-fatiguing)
- If you tested strength markers earlier in the week, you can re-check 1–2 of them on Day 4 or Day 5 at very light loads (RPE 6–7) to monitor trends without adding fatigue.
- Suggested markers to monitor without adding fatigue:
  - Floor press variant rep max test: 2 sets to post a controlled 4–6 rep max at ~70% of planned 1RM.
  - 3RM or 4–5RM on a leg/hip hinge movement with light loading: attempt 1–2 technically crisp attempts.
  - Barbell Row or chest-supported row rep max: 1–2 attempts with a light, controlled load.

Recovery and ancillary components
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
- Hydration: 3–4 liters/day (adjust for body size/climate)
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes post-workout, focusing on hips, thoracic spine, shoulders
- Shoulder health: continue scapular control and external rotation work 2–3 times per week

Notes for implementation
- If any day feels too aggressive for the client, dial back by removing the extra push progression on Day 3 and revert to the original light deload structure (9 total sets on lifting days, 60–90 seconds rest between sets).
- If the client’s schedule requires more adjustment, you can shift Day 3’s mobility to another day and keep push progression limited to Days 4–5.

Here is the full deload week with all adjustments rolled in:

Assumptions
- Prior program: 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy, ~18 working sets per session.
- Deload target: ~40–50% of prior weekly volume, with movements preserved but loads and sets reduced.
- Shoulder-friendly chest emphasis replaces traditional bench press.
- Mobility day added (20 minutes) plus two Zone 2 cardio sessions.
- Midweek push progression on Days 3 and 5 to address boredom, kept within deload safety.
- Weekly structure: 7 days with 5 training/light activity days and 2 rest days (or adjust to your schedule; reflect this cadence).

Weekly structure at a glance
- Day 1: Upper 1 (shoulder-friendly chest emphasis)
- Day 2: Lower 1 (quad-dominant)
- Day 3: Mobility & Active Recovery + Light midweek push progression
- Day 4: Upper 2 (pull/push balance)
- Day 5: Lower 2 (posterior chain emphasis) – uptick in intensity relative to Day 2
- Day 6: Zone 2 Cardio 30 minutes
- Day 7: Rest or Active Recovery

Day-by-day plan with exact sets/reps and loads guidance

Day 1 – Upper 1 (shoulder-friendly chest emphasis)
- Dumbbell Floor Press (neutral grip or flat, depending on comfort): 3 sets x 5 reps at RPE 6
- Overhead Press (light, seated or dumbbell): 2 sets x 6 reps at RPE 6
- Incline Dumbbell Press: 1 set x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Dumbbell Row: 2 sets x 8 reps
- Lateral Raises: 1 set x 12 reps
- Plank: 2 sets x 30 seconds
Total working sets: 9
Notes:
- If shoulder irritates, reduce Overhead Press to 1 set x 6, or swap to a light Dumbbell Arnold press with a very light load.
- Tempo targets: 2-0-2-0 for all pressing movements; 2-1-2-0 for rows if desired.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between sets; 2–3 minutes for any heavier set if needed.

Day 2 – Lower 1 (quad-dominant)
- Back Squat or Goblet Squat (as needed for comfort): 3 sets x 5 reps at RPE 6
- Leg Press: 1 set x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Walking Lunges: 1 set x 8 reps per leg at RPE 6
- Leg Extension: 1 set x 12 reps at RPE 6
- Romanian Deadlift or Hyperextensions (light): 1 set x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Farmer’s Carry: 1 set x 30 seconds
Total: 9
Notes:
- If barbell back squat is uncomfortable, substitute goblet squat or DB front squat to preserve knee/hip drive.
- Focus on technique and depth within comfort.

Day 3 – Mobility & Active Recovery + Light Push Progression (midweek push)
- Mobility session: 20 minutes (as outlined previously; hips, thoracic, shoulders, ankles)
- Light push work (optional, total 3–4 extra working sets maximum):
  - Dumbbell Floor Press: 2 sets x 6 reps at RPE 7
  - Incline Dumbbell Press: 1 set x 6 reps at RPE 7
Notes:
- If shoulder fatigued, drop to RPE 6 or skip the extra push work entirely.
- Tempo: 2-0-2-0 for presses.
- This day should feel controlled and non-fatiguing.

Day 4 – Upper 2 (pull/push balance)
- Barbell Row: 3 sets x 5–6 reps at RPE 6
- Push-ups or Dumbbell Floor Press: 2 sets x 6–8 reps at RPE 6–7 (choose option that preserves shoulder comfort)
- Seated Cable Face Pulls: 1–2 sets x 12 reps
- Dumbbell Hammer Curls: 1–2 sets x 10 reps
- Tricep Pushdowns: 1–2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Pallof Press: 2 sets x 12 reps per side
Total: 9
Notes:
- If push movements aggravate, swap to a machine chest press with neutral grip and keep reps conservative.

Day 5 – Lower 2 (posterior chain emphasis) – uptick
- Deadlift (light-to-moderate, emphasize form): 3 sets x 4–5 reps at RPE 6–7
- Glute-Ham Raise or Romanian Deadlift (light): 1–2 sets x 8 reps at RPE 6
- Leg Curl: 1–2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Cable Pull-Through: 1–2 sets x 12 reps
- Core (Bird Dogs or Dead Bug): 2 sets x 12 reps per side
Total: 9
Notes:
- If deadlift form is unstable, drop to 3x4 at RPE 6 or reduce to 3x3 with a lighter load.

Day 6 – Zone 2 Cardio 30 minutes
- Zone 2 cardio: 30 minutes continuous (walk, cycle, or row at a comfortable but steady pace)
Notes:
- Keep the effort conversational; you can break into two 15-minute blocks if needed by schedule.

Day 7 – Rest or Active Recovery
- Optional light cardio, mobility work, or complete rest
Notes:
- Use this day to check in on shoulder comfort and overall recovery. Hydrate, sleep, and nutrition remain important.

Strength markers testing (deload-friendly and non-fatiguing)
- If you tested strength markers earlier in the week, you can re-check 1–2 of them on Day 4 or Day 5 at very light loads (RPE 6–7) to monitor trends without adding fatigue.
- Suggested markers to monitor without adding fatigue:
  - Floor press variant rep max test: 2 sets to post a controlled 4–6 rep max at ~70% of planned 1RM.
  - 3RM or 4–5RM on a leg/hip hinge movement with light loading: attempt 1–2 technically crisp attempts.
  - Barbell Row or chest-supported row rep max: 1–2 attempts with a light, controlled load.

Recovery and ancillary components
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
- Hydration: 3–4 liters/day (adjust for body size/climate)
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes post-workout, focusing on hips, thoracic spine, shoulders
- Shoulder health: continue scapular control and external rotation work 2–3 times per week

Notes for implementation
- If any day feels too aggressive for the client, dial back by removing the extra push progression on Day 3 and revert to the original light deload structure (9 total sets on lifting days, 60–90 seconds rest between sets).
- If the client’s schedule requires more adjustment, you can shift Day 3’s mobility to another day and keep push progression limited to Days 4–5.
